section_title: What should shape our thoughts and actions?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 8 Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable—if anything is excellent or praiseworthy—think on these things. 9 Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me, put it into practice. And the God of peace will be with you.

context_lines: After encouraging prayer and promising God’s guarding peace, Paul turns to what should occupy their minds. He names what is true, honorable, right, pure, lovely and admirable—what deserves careful attention.

The next verse carries thought into action. They are to practice what they learned and received from him, including what they heard and saw in his life. The letter has already supplied examples of service, endurance and putting others first.
This is more than imagining pleasant outcomes. Paul joins attention to what is good with the work of living it. The passage ends with the promise that the God of peace will be with them.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand these verses as a call to direct both thought and conduct toward what is good. [Wesley’s notes on verses 8–9](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-epistle-to-the-philippians/) connect reflection with practice and emphasize God Himself as the source of peace. The [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/philippians/4) connect Paul’s appeal to the faithful example he commends in 3:17. The focus is a formed way of life, rather than thought detached from action.
god_plan_lines: [Romans 12:1–3](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/12.htm) places the renewing of the mind within a whole life offered to God in response to His mercy. It connects changed thinking with recognizing His will and living humbly among others.

That renewal belongs within God’s purpose to make His people like His Son, stated in [Romans 8:29–30](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/8.htm). The thoughts and habits described here are part of a life being shaped toward Christ, with its completion still ahead.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
